feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: U.S. envoys visit Kyiv for first time after meeting Putin in Moscow
entry.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff made their first trip to Kyiv, one day after meeting Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

entry.title: The price of diesel is showing up in the price of almost everything
entry.summary: Diesel has hit a record high. Stephan Bisaha visits an Alabama truck stop to talk with drivers and business owners about how high prices are changing what they spend and charge.

entry.title: A trucker explains what record diesel prices mean for his business
entry.summary: Monte Wiederhold runs a trucking company in northwest Ohio. He explains how problems overseas affect businesses at home.

entry.title: Shipping companies are putting sails back on cargo ships
entry.summary: One of the world's largest logistics companies plans to fit one of its ships with a strange type of sail, the latest in a small but growing number of cleaner sailing shipping vessels.

entry.title: Bad news about ticks: cold weather may not stop them
entry.summary: Ticks and the diseases they carry are a growing problem nationwide. As tick season ends, a closer look at what researchers are learning about how ticks survive and spread disease.

entry.title: Meet the alien math-rock duo selling out shows across the U.S.
entry.summary: Angine de Poitrine wears giant masks, speaks an alien language and plays wildly complicated math rock. Manager Sebastien Collin talks about the rise of the enigmatic musical group.

entry.title: Cineplexity: The movies that tried to make sense of 9/11
entry.summary: Over the past quarter century the events of 9/11 have been reflected in direct and indirect ways in movies.

entry.title: What Russia and China learned from America after 9/11
entry.summary: Journalists Mikhail Zygar and Cindy Yu explain how the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan helped reshape Russia and China's ambitions.

entry.title: Author Emily Wilson on how she brings Homer's ancient poems back to life
entry.summary: Classicist Emily Wilson talks about her new book, 'Crossing the Wine Dark Sea,' a series of essays reflecting on translation and classic writing in the modern world.

entry.title: U.S. Forest Service to keep some research stations open, after pushback about restructuring
entry.summary: In a massive restructuring under the Trump administration, U.S. Forest Service is closing dozens of research stations but, as NPR's Chiara Eisner reports, it is keeping some facilities open that had been projected to shutter.
